category.name: Commission, Decommission and Dispose of Assets

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Citation statuses observe source_status_ceiling. 19.1 is APQC 10.2.6, GFMAM 6.2 and ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.1, with 18.4.4 as the clearance producer. 19.2 is 49 CFR 192.727 and 192.629 for gas, 16 U.S.C. 824o for the electric absence, APQC 10.4.2/10.4.4 and GFMAM 6.7. 19.3 is 40 CFR 761.50/60/61/62/65/40/180 and 40 CFR 262.11/262.20/268.1. 19.4 is 18 CFR 101 EPI 10 and Definition 34, 18 CFR 125.3 Item 16(b), APQC 10.4.3. 12.1.6 retires the register; 5.3 unitises additions; 5.1.1 closes the work; 10.6.5 and 10.6.7 stay on the customer side of 19.1.3.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: 19.2.6 and 12.2.3 look like one act: both update the spatial network after an asset change. Split proposed: 19.2.6 produces as-left connectivity from the field; 12.2.3 publishes that accepted change into the spatial system of record. Written that way here. If the taxonomy keeps both names, the split has to live in the specs or one of them is a duplicate.

19.2.5 and 12.1.6 look like one act: both close the asset after it leaves service. Split: 19.2.5 produces physical disposition evidence (and 192.727(g) where it bites); 12.1.6 end-dates the register and maintenance eligibility. ChatGPT already wrote 12.1.6 that way. The process NAME 'Retire and dispose of assets' on 12.1.6 remains misleading, as that specification already said.
19.4.3 and 5.3 look like one act on the property record. Split: 5.3 unitises ADDITIONS of completed construction; 19.4.3 retires the unit under 18 CFR 101 EPI 10 and Definition 34. Both stay.
19.1.1 and 5.1.1 look like one act on completion evidence. Split: 5.1.1 verifies the WORK is done; 19.1.1 accepts the ASSET into commissioning. A closed work order is not commissioned plant.

19.1.3 and 19.1.4 could collapse into 'energise it'. Split held: 19.1.3 consumes 18.4.4 and the 18.2.2 window (coordination); 19.1.4 is first energise and performance. APQC already split them as 10.2.6.2 and a following activity. Same shape as 17.5.2 owning the arithmetic and 17.2.2 weighing it.

19.2.4 and 19.4.1 could collapse into 'what happens to the asset'. Split held: 19.2.4 is the PHYSICAL end-state under 192.727 (or operator method for electric); 19.4.1 is where TITLE goes (scrap, sell, trade, transfer) under 18 CFR 101 or the contract.

8.6.6, 18.4.3 and 19.2.3 all purge. Split already in the APQC crosswalk for 8.6.6 vs 19.2.4: 8.6.6 is in-service pressure work; 18.4.3 purges a section that will RETURN; 19.2.3 purges plant that is LEAVING. Three processes, one 192.629, three purposes. Recorded rather than merged.

16 U.S.C. 824o(a)(1) means there is no federal electric-distribution abandonment, purge, commissioning-test or retention rule. 19.2.3, 19.2.4 and 19.4.4 return that absence as a class with that statute, they do not invent an electric 192.727.
APQC 10.4.1 Develop exit strategy (pcf_id 10952) is crosswalked as scope. Not added. Portfolio exit remains 17.2.6 / 17.4, not a fifth group here.
IEC 61968-11 Work package has no CommissioningRecord, WasteClass or RetirementUnit class. Held as WorkActivityRecord, WorkAsset and Asset.

EN 17007 SPP.12 is disposal of faulty or damaged spare items. Abandoning a main and shipping PCB oil are both mapped to it as nearest process. ISO 55001 cl. 8.1 and GFMAM 6.7 are the real spine for 19.2-19.4.

40 CFR 112 SPCC is facility-level, pack-scoped as not job-level. Not cited for 19.3. State waste codes and TSCA 761 concentration arithmetic beyond the 50 ppm trigger in 761.50(a)(4) are not reproduced.
